shapes.html: The function run lifts single-step behaviour to a sequence of reactions.
Unfold the inputs and component uses along logical time; then fold them into a recurring process.

notes: We have controlled one application. The next step is to apply a component over a sequence of inputs. This is the role of run. Read the major arguments without reading every symbol.

The input sequence has length n. We provide n linear uses of the component and an initial state. These are uses over time, not a commitment to n physical copies. For repeated f, these resources are uses of that transition function; bare resource counting alone does not prove their behavioural equality.

Each illustrated reaction takes the next input and the available state, then produces an output and the state passed forward. Follow the actual token identities. The same state thread connects the reactions.

Follow the next reaction and state thread. Animation duration does not denote physical execution time. The one-input-per-iteration restriction is explained on P13 and is not imposed by the signature alone.

The same state thread connects these later and final reactions. The type describes finite input/output vectors of the same arbitrary length n, rather than unqualified infinite streams. The thesis gives the full typed construction in section 3.3.1.

We have drawn these uses along logical time. We can fold this unfolded view into a recurring process. Do not manually perform the next Morph here. Advance to P13, retaining this final geometry as its starting view.
